title: SEO and GEO: where should your business start?
summary: Start with a useful, discoverable website. Then build the clarity and credibility that support both traditional and AI search.
author: ARA Editorial
answer: Start with the foundations: clear service pages, accessible content, accurate business details and a website that works well on mobile. These support both SEO and visibility in AI search.

sections.heading: What is the difference?
paragraphs: SEO helps search engines discover and understand useful pages. GEO is a term used for work aimed at improving visibility in generative AI search experiences. The two share much of the same foundation.
For a small business, this means you do not need two disconnected websites or two competing content strategies. Start by explaining what you do, who you help and what the next step looks like.

sections.heading: Make your services specific
paragraphs: A page called Services is a starting point, but customers often need more detail. A renovation business might explain kitchen renovations, its service area, the enquiry process and the information required to prepare a quote.
Use real information. A clear explanation of a service is more useful than a page repeating a location and a keyword without answering any questions.

sections.heading: Remove technical obstacles
paragraphs: Check that important pages can be reached through ordinary links, return successful responses and contain readable content. Make navigation and enquiry forms usable on a phone.

Google’s guidance says that its generative AI search features build on its existing search systems. There is no special AI schema required, and an llms.txt file is not a requirement for appearing in Google Search.

sections.heading: Publish what your customers need to know
paragraphs: Write from your own expertise. Explain the decisions customers face, show your actual process and distinguish examples from completed client work. Keep business details consistent and update content when the underlying information changes.
A useful article should leave someone better equipped to make a decision. Avoid producing many similar pages solely to target variations of the same search query.

sections.heading: Measure progress without making promises
paragraphs: Once your public website and Search Console are configured, track the pages people discover and the enquiries that follow. Record the starting point, the changes made and the questions still unanswered.
No agency can guarantee that a page will be indexed, rank in a particular position or be cited by an AI system. A sensible plan focuses on work you can verify and improvements you can maintain.
